title: Build-time gates on the VPS, landing gate on the Mac
what: `relay gate` during a build sends the committed head to the VPS over ssh (a non-root account), runs the pinned gate there and records its log so the cycle's gate, fix-gate and check steps read it; the landing gate (`relay land`) still runs on the Mac and alone decides the merge. Falls back to the Mac when the VPS cannot be reached. Prerequisites: the clean-Linux quick gate green (item the-quick-gate-is-red-again-in-a-clean-linux-ima), a non-root account on the VPS with the pinned Python and tools in its home, no change to the VPS's services (gitea, woodpecker, dockerd, a GitHub Actions runner run there as root).
why: Owner, 30 Oct, answered "a" to: should a gate on the VPS ai.amidman.com decide the gates run while a change is built, with the Mac running only the landing gate. Measured the same day: one git start 27 ms on the loaded Mac vs 1.5 ms on the VPS; three git-heavy test files 158 s vs 34 s; 4.8 gates per landed change today, so Mac gates per change would drop to 1 (about 79% fewer Mac gate minutes).
pass_cases: A build-time gate of a change runs on the VPS and its result is what the cycle's review and check read.
The merge hook accepts a landing only on a Mac gate log of the landed head.
With the VPS unreachable, the gate runs on the Mac and says so in one line.

fact: Design vps-build-gates rev 2 (30 Oct; reviewed: 1 HIGH, 7 MEDIUM, 2 LOW, all fixed in the revision). Build about 4 h 50 min of agent time in 5 changes. Key points: each build-time gate runs relay's tests in a fresh rootless podman container on the VPS with no network and no host folder mounted, at most 2 at once, cpu_shares 256 below the server's services (caddy, forgejo, woodpecker with an ALIX agent, mailserver, a site: together ~0.9 GB RAM, under 1.2% CPU when read); the image is built only from the default branch's recipe (about 4-5 builds a week, the only step with network); a remote log never decides a merge (the merge hook reads only the Mac log); after each landing one VPS gate runs on the new default branch head, and a red one becomes one fix item at the top of the queue, while other lanes gate on the Mac. Front decisions (owner can reverse): images only from the default branch's recipe; lanes gate on the Mac while the default branch is red on Linux.

question: May relay set up the gate account on ai.amidman.com itself, using the owner's root login: create the account relay-gate (no admin rights, no docker access), its .ssh folder and relay's key line, each command shown before it runs, undone by deleting the account?
options: a. relay does it: the owner says yes once; 3 commands as root, once.
b. The owner runs the same 3 commands and pastes one key.
reading: relay creates the relay-gate account on ai.amidman.com itself with the owner's root login (3 commands, once, each shown before it runs).

question: Does the VPS gate build take one lane now, ahead of the queue's fixes, or wait its turn after the 39 open fixes (about 23 agent hours by the queue's estimates, roughly a day at today's pace of about 1.5 landings an hour)?
options: a. One lane now for the VPS build (changes 2-4 in sequence, about 4 h agent time, ~6-8 h wall with reviews; bring-up after the clean-Linux fix): five lanes keep fixing; later gates on the VPS speed every change.
b. Strict order: fixes first; the VPS build starts in about a day.
answer: a, разве мы не приняли решение 3 на 3 ?
reading: Option a: the VPS build takes a lane now. The owner recalls the recorded 29 Oct decision: 3 lanes for relay's development (product features, the container gate on top) and 3 for fixes. The front had filled all 6 lanes with fixes; the lane pick offers fixes only, so the split was lost.

fact: 30 Oct ~06:20Z: the landing gate of wt/the-quick-gate-is-red-again-in-a-clean-l went red on this Mac with one library-test error, BlockingIOError [Errno 35] Resource temporarily unavailable (a git process could not be started, 834 s step); 6 lanes and 2 gate slots were busy. A red that found nothing wrong in the code; the landing was run again. Evidence for moving gates to the VPS (process start 0.7 ms there vs 5-10 ms here).
